title: Halcyon FX week 6 live: 12 trades, −$37.45, a rough week (and what I found wrong)
author: Teh_Eno
selftext:
Disclosure: I built this EA and sell it.

Halcyon has been about a year in development, with many iterations. It's been running live since mid-Sep 2026, and these are the real results. It's AI-backed: a local bridge asks Claude to confirm or veto each entry, and the AI can only block trades, never create them.

Week of Mon 19 to Sun 25 Oct (Sydney time), closed trades

LIVE account:

* 12 trades: 5 wins, 7 losses
* Net −$37.45 (−3.42%)
* Profit factor 0.49
* Max closed-trade drawdown $47.01 (4.30%)

DEMO account (runs a more permissive lab build):

* 25 trades: 10 wins, 15 losses
* Net −$979.22 (−5.73%)
* Profit factor 0.63
* Max closed-trade drawdown $1,084.44 (6.31%)

LIVE running total since 14 Sep: 47 trades, 26 wins and 21 losses, −$15.15, PF 0.93.

What happened: Three trades held over the previous weekend closed on Monday's open. One had locked in a profit and gapped through to a −1.22R loss. A broker outage on 20 Oct left one trade unmanaged until its stop hit. I closed two winners manually on 20 Oct, which cost a bit compared with letting the EA run them. The biggest losers were two Friday JPY-cross buys taken just under demand zones that had already broken.

What I found wrong with the zone logic: Digging into those losses turned up several real problems in how the EA handles supply and demand zones.

* Orders in reverse. It could buy into supply or sell into demand. After a demand zone broke, price went back into it and was rejected about 4 times, and the EA still bought. Broken zones never flipped sides, when a broken demand zone should become supply and a broken supply zone should become demand.
* Duplicate boxes. Several overlapping zones were drawn at the same level, and old zones overlapped newer opposite ones.
* Zones found badly. The pivot scan depth, rejection confirmation and touch counting were all off.
* No room-to-target check. The EA can trade between zones, or into an opposing zone, because it doesn't require clear room to the target. Only a basic H4 trend check exists, not a check against real higher-timeframe zones.
* Missed breaks. On 23 Sep it missed sells at H1 demand breaks that I could see on the chart, because it never formed those candidates.
* The AI couldn't see key levels. The EA calculated unfilled gaps, equal highs and lows, and previous day and week highs and lows, but the old bridge ignored them. As of this morning (26 Oct) the AI sees them as information only. It can't override the hard rules, and the first real request after the swap hasn't been confirmed yet.

Where the fixes stand: A new DEMO build (8.91d) has a hard block on buying into supply or selling into demand that no AI score can override, plus zone flipping, one box per spot, and six entry fixes from an audit. It's built and checked, but it only runs on DEMO and is not proven live yet. The market was shut when it loaded. The room-to-target and higher-timeframe zone check isn't built yet.

LIVE is paused for me. The LIVE build (8.580) went live on 19 Oct with a rollover shield for the daily spread spike. It has been off since 25 Oct because it isn't profitable and doesn't have the fixes above. It won't go back on until the fixes have been proven on DEMO.

There are still users who have preferred to continue with the build running, and some have not occurred the losses I have as different brokers do act differently.  But they also understand the risks associated with continuing to run the current build.

With only 5 to 12 trades a week, one week can swing PF from about 0.2 to over 4, so neither good nor bad weeks say much until it's past a hundred or so trades. I'll keep posting every week, rough ones included.

Not financial advice. Trading forex is risky, past results don't guarantee future ones, and you can lose money.

comments.body: rough week but this is the honest kind of post. same thing I said at week 4 though, 47 trades is still too few to tell a bad week from a broken edge. the more useful log might be the entries Claude vetoed, and what they would have done.
